issues.description: RevokeErr exposed without specification of what it may contain
issues.detail: The author themselves asks in the PR description: 'Is it safe to display the revoke error? It could contain sensitive information.' This is precisely the unreasoned condition Dijkstra refuses. The precondition for exposing RevokeErr to an API consumer must be stated and proven: that no code path writes secrets, tokens, or backend-internal addresses into this string. 'It should not' is not a proof.

issues.description: Function renamed but metric label and stale comment remain
issues.detail: FetchLeaseInfo still emits the metric 'expire.fetch-lease-times' and the test TestExpiration_FetchLeaseTimesIrrevocable retains its old name. The rename claims a broader postcondition (returns 'non sensitive information' rather than times), but observable identifiers were not updated. Either the rename was cosmetic or the metric is now mislabeled. Pick one and be consistent.

issues.description: Postcondition of leaseInfoForExport is not stated and not enforced
issues.detail: The comment promises a 'redacted leaseEntry' but the function is an allowlist by enumeration with no invariant tying it to leaseEntry's fields. When a future field is added to leaseEntry, nothing forces a decision about whether it is sensitive. The redaction property must be expressed structurally (e.g., a typed projection) or asserted in a test that fails when leaseEntry grows.

issues.description: Test asserts presence of path but not absence of sensitive fields
issues.detail: TestSystemBackend_leases adds a single equality check for path='secret/foo'. There is no test asserting that Secret.InternalData, ClientToken, Auth, or other sensitive members are absent from the response. Testing shows the presence of bugs; here it does not even attempt to show the absence of leakage. The redaction claim is untested.

issues.description: Namespace exposure lacks an authorization invariant
issues.detail: namespace_path is now returned whenever leaseInfo.namespace.Path is non-empty. No reasoning is presented about whether a caller in namespace A looking up a lease ID should learn the full path of namespace B, nor whether the existing ACL on leases/lookup already enforces this. The invariant 'caller is authorized to know this namespace path' should be stated and shown to hold.

issues.description: Context substitution in test changes semantics silently
issues.detail: TestExpiration_revokeEntry_rejected_fairsharing swaps namespace.RootContext(nil) for namespace.RootContext(t.Context()). This is an unrelated drive-by change buried in a rename commit. Either it fixes a real cancellation/timeout bug, in which case it deserves its own justification, or it is noise. Mixing it in obscures the diff and the reasoning.

review.summary: The change is small but its author already telegraphed the unreasoned bit: 'Is it safe to display the revoke error?' That question must be answered before merge, not after. The rename from FetchLeaseTimes to FetchLeaseInfo widens the postcondition without stating it, and the redaction property of leaseInfoForExport is an enumeration with no structural guarantee against future leakage. Tests assert presence of the new fields but never the absence of sensitive ones — the canonical confusion of testing with proof. REASONED in shape, UNREASONED on the security-relevant boundary it crosses. Refused until the precondition on RevokeErr content is stated and the redaction invariant is enforced rather than enumerated.
